findings: Both captures document a server-side HTTP 402 challenge and a receipt-bearing resource response on verified payment. November spells out an agent authorizing payment and retrying with a credential, and illustrates the server recording a PaymentIntent with Stripe before returning the resource. The challenge, authorization and retry are separate from verified payment and on-chain/offramp settlement. No checkout UI is involved (old raw lines 130-195, new raw lines 5-21 and 62-97).

The November Node handler uses mppx and Stripe, a server secret key, a Stripe profile ID as networkId and defaultMethods(). It derives the example challenge key from the Stripe secret via HMAC instead of the older random 32-byte secret. It derives livemode from the key marker in the shown handler, with the sandbox profile and optional Tempo-path setup described separately. Business Profiles retrieval and standalone Crypto Deposit Address REST examples pin 2026-07-29.preview. The November SDK constructor shown does not pin that version for every request (old raw lines 18-22, 47-68, 130-163 and new raw lines 23-36, 54-97, 107-152 and 222-237).

The shared November endpoint starts with SPTs. Configuring a created or fetched Tempo address enables Tempo in defaultMethods(). The combined handler example uses 0.50 USD for both methods, while compose() allows different prices per method. Separate floors are 0.50 USD for SPT card payments and 0.01 USDC for stablecoins, and the guide distinguishes Tempo transfers in USDC.e. Stripe says it offramps supported stablecoin payments and settles to Stripe balance (new raw lines 36 and 99-152). Earlier samples use two $1 Hono GET routes (old raw lines 130-195).

The May quickstart explicitly requires crypto payins to be enabled on the Stripe account (old raw lines 18-22). November's dedicated MPP guide documents endpoint configuration and defers eligibility to the separate Machine Payments overview. The sandbox key and profile_test_ are environment-specific. Stripe recommends keeping deposit address provisioning or retrieval calls off the core request path (new raw lines 107-133).

Stripe-hosted Tempo fee sponsorship is optional with mppx 0.9.2 or later, hostedFeePayer=true, live mode, a Tempo deposit address from the same account as the API key, and no Connect integration. Customers still sign and authorize (new raw lines 154-172).

The November guide adds discovery/challenge/error/full-flow checks with mppx validate, manual Link CLI test SPT and Tempo CLI routes and a sandbox using a test key and profile_test_, with a sandbox Tempo address when exercising the Tempo path. Its example testing URL uses POST /paid while the code is an exported handler, so do not infer a router declaration or carry over May's separate GET paths. It explicitly says live validation can use real funds and a live Tempo address in manual testing moves real funds (old raw lines 144-204, new raw lines 90-97 and 174-237).

Current summary line 18 conflates detection and lookup. The old sample's Credential.extractPaymentScheme checks the header scheme, Credential.fromRequest extracts the challenge recipient, and NodeCache membership gates reuse. An uncached recipient or unexpected missing deposit details throws. The 5-minute NodeCache TTL and distributed cache recommendation are May implementation advice, while the chain-specific PATH_USD constant belongs to the old testnet example (old raw lines 62-128 and 142-173).

The HTTP 402/credential/retry/verified resource and receipt sequence remains (old raw lines 34-68, 73-128 and 130-205, new raw lines 23-36 and 62-97).

The example deposit workflow changes from creating a deposit-mode PaymentIntent per initial crypto flow to creating or fetching a Tempo deposit address through the Crypto Deposit Addresses API and supplying the stored address. Keeping those calls off the core request path is Stripe's recommendation. November previews cover profile/address REST calls rather than the May direct Stripe client pin (old raw lines 18-30 and 53-128, new raw lines 28-34 and 107-152).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-machine-mpp-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-machine-payments-mpp-quickstart-2026.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-machine-payments-mpp-quickstart.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/mpp`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/mpp, the November capture documents API agents paying without a checkout UI. The server returns an HTTP 402 challenge, the agent authorizes payment and retries with a payment credential, and the verified flow returns the resource and receipt. The diagram shows the server recording the payment as a Stripe PaymentIntent (new raw lines 5-21 and new raw lines 62-97). The server uses mppx and Stripe and supplies its Stripe profile ID as networkId. By default the shown handler supports card SPTs. Configuring a separately created or fetched Tempo deposit address adds stablecoin payments to the same handler. Stripe recommends keeping those address API calls off the core request path (new raw lines 107-133). The separate November Machine Payments overview specifies account-level Stablecoins and Crypto enablement in Dashboard and Stripe review and approval before activation (raw/stripe-payments-machine-2026-11-07.md:41-56). The card SPT minimum is 0.50 USD and the stablecoin minimum is 0.01 USDC, with Tempo transferring USDC.e and Stripe describing off-ramp to its balance. The handler example charges 0.50 USD for either enabled method (new raw lines 23-36 and new raw lines 99-152). Sandbox uses a test key and sandbox profile. A sandbox Tempo address is for exercising the Tempo path. The shown default SPT handler has no crypto address in its configuration (new raw lines 62-105 and new raw lines 222-237). Live-mode Tempo fee sponsorship needs mppx 0.9.2 or later and a deposit address and API key from the same account, excludes Connect, and preserves customer authorization (new raw lines 154-184 and new raw lines 222-237). The mapped source-stripe-machine-payments-mpp-quickstart.md describes the May two-route Hono example with $1 card/Link and Tempo flows, PaymentIntent-derived crypto addresses, five-minute NodeCache recipient reuse, and a 2026-03-04.preview client pin. The May quickstart also explicitly requires crypto payins to be enabled on the Stripe account, a prerequisite omitted by the mapped summary (old raw lines 18-22). Those details remain dated May evidence (old raw lines 18-30, old raw lines 47-128 and old raw lines 130-205).
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/mpp, the November operational changes missing from source-stripe-machine-payments-mpp-quickstart.md are the profile-backed stripe.create/defaultMethods wrapper, a server HMAC-derived challenge secret, a configured Tempo address with provisioning or lookup recommended off the core request path, method-specific minima and optional mppx 0.9.2-plus live Tempo fee sponsorship. The REST profile/address examples use 2026-07-29.preview, while the new SDK constructor shown has no explicit version pin (new raw lines 23-36, new raw lines 68-97 and new raw lines 107-172). Retain May's separate Hono GET handlers, its historical 'internal' SPT sample, random challenge secret, testnet token, direct deposit-mode PaymentIntent and cache, and 2026-03-04.preview client pin (old raw lines 18-30, old raw lines 47-128 and old raw lines 130-205). The title, new explanatory diagram and links primarily change presentation. Keep reciprocal source and concept warnings for the configured deposit address versus per-payment generation, the dated May sandbox PaymentIntent simulation versus November validate/testnet setup, and the product-level Connect support versus the hosted fee-payer exclusion. The reciprocal Machine Payments concept and overview source should qualify their 'just a crypto wallet' agent description (wiki/concepts/stripe-machine-payments.md:14-16 and wiki/sources/source-stripe-machine-payments.md:15-20). A wallet serves the stablecoin route. The SPT rail uses an SPT credential, and the November manual example obtains a one-time test token via Link CLI and a Link account. That example supplies a test provisioning method. Both rails are also present in May (new raw lines 99-109, new raw lines 186-220 and old raw lines 130-195). Separate older geographic descriptions from the related November availability guidance. Retain test-key/profile matching and the possibility of real funds in live validation or manual Tempo use (new raw lines 99-105 and new raw lines 154-237). Challenge and receipt handling, documented settlement, and observed live payment are separate status and evidence boundaries.
